youtube_title: You Signed the Gym Waiver. In New York, That May Not Protect the Gym 🦝⚖️
caption: New York General Obligations Law 5-326 voids waivers at paid recreational facilities that try to excuse the operator's own negligence. Injury alone isn't negligence, and not every program is covered.
script: In New York, that gym waiver you signed might be legally meaningless. [disclaimer] Yes, the one you signed without reading! New York has a law aimed at this exact kind of fine print. If you pay to use a pool, a gym, an amusement park, or a place like that, any deal that says the owner isn't responsible for their own carelessness, or their staff's carelessness, is void. It's against public policy. It doesn't count! So picture this. You pay for a gym membership. You sign a waiver that says the gym isn't responsible for anything. The law only covers certain places you pay to have fun at. Not every sports form or class falls under it. And getting hurt doesn't prove the gym messed up. You still have to show the gym was careless, and that the carelessness actually caused your injury. And the gym can still argue you accepted the normal risks of working out.
